Mr. Sultan Husain Khan, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, who appeared for the Respondents submitted that the suit instituted by the appellant had, in effect, challenged the acquisition of rent receiving interests by the Government under the provisions of the aforesaid Act. Since, according to him, after the notifications of acquisition of non-retainable khas lands, any application for retaining such land in excess of the question relating to acquisition. He strenuously attempted to convince us of the applicability of Art. 2 of the President's Order No.90 of 1972 to the appellant's prayer for declaring as illegal the order of refusal to grant certificate under Section 20(4) of the Act. On its applicability the appellant's suit, it is obvious, cannot stand. 

 6. To appreciate the respective contentions of the learned Counsel, it is necessary to understand the nature of right claimed by the appellant. There is no dispute that they cannot retain any khas land in excess of the limit specified in Section 20(2) of the Act.
